gen-fs-quilon-fs-asap: Asap reads crisp and businesslike, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. And Quilon above it swells and thins gently, so a long page of text would feel steady under a commanding headline.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads friendly and a bit loose, curvy letters drawn with one wire-thin line throughout. Quilon, by contrast, lets each letter's stroke swell and slim quietly, so the two share a page with plenty of texture.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-fira-sans: Commanding, with an editorial streak, Quilon takes the top spot here. Fira Sans brings a tall x-height and a drafting-pen line with no thick-thin shifts, which is the quality that makes the pair feel so purposeful.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-merriweather-sans: Quilon opens the page with an editorial voice, its thin strokes only slightly lighter than the thick ones. Merriweather Sans follows with sturdy, tall lowercase and a clearly open e, so the two fit together without fuss.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-supreme: Quilon carries an editorial, commanding tone, with modest contrast you only notice when you look closely at its curves. Supreme brings crisp, heavy-looking text.
gen-fs-quilon-general-sans: Quilon heads things off with moderate thick-thin shifts and a commanding editorial manner. General Sans then runs the text at a smooth, contrast-free line, so a long stretch of reading would glide along.
gen-fs-quilon-manrope: Manrope has bright gaps at every curve and a line that looks bent from wire, held to one width throughout. A long read would feel light and friendly.
gen-fs-quilon-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall in the line, its wide-open e never squeezed and every stroke cut as if with one marker tip. A long stretch of it would read smoothly and warmly.
gen-fs-quilon-work-sans: Work Sans sets a modern, contemporary text with c tips that stay well apart and one stroke width running through the whole alphabet. Quilon does its best work at the top, where its bowls thin gracefully into an editorial headline, while Work Sans simply keeps the text steady.
gen-eater-fs-nunito: Eater brings a dark, aggressive headline, with modest stem-to-hairline contrast and short ascenders against its wide gaps. Nunito softens the page below with round lowercase bowls and terminals that stop clear of the stem.
